claims.text: The ability of CrFeCoNiX alloys to form a stable, coherent protective oxide above 900 °C is primarily governed by the identity of X.
X governs oxidation behavior through its effects on oxide–substrate lattice matching and diffusion kinetics.
Al addition preferentially promotes formation of a dense, continuous Al2O3 scale.
The Al2O3 scale has low lattice mismatch with the CrFeCoNiAl substrate.
The Al2O3 scale has minimal or lower thermal-expansion mismatch with the metallic substrate.
Al addition increases adhesion of the oxide scale to the substrate.
Al-derived interfacial diffusion barriers reduce diffusion rates at the oxide–metal interface.
Reduced interfacial diffusion and improved lattice fit limit oxide-scale strain accumulation.
Si or Mn additions favor mixed or less densely packed oxide scales.
Oxides formed in the Si- or Mn-containing alloys have higher interfacial strain and less controlled growth kinetics than the Al-containing alloy.
Higher interfacial stresses in Si- or Mn-containing alloys make their oxide scales more likely to crack or spall during thermal cycling.
Under identical high-temperature oxidative conditions, CrFeCoNiAl will form a more stable, coherent, adherent, and less defective oxide scale than CrFeCoNiSi, CrFeCoNiMn, or CrFeCoNi.
CrFeCoNiSi, CrFeCoNiMn, and the CrFeCoNi baseline will exhibit less coherent scaling and more cracking or spallation than CrFeCoNiAl.
The proposed behavior applies above 900 °C in oxidizing or corrosive atmospheres for alloys in single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution states.
Casting defects, porosity, or other significant processing-induced microstructural changes may alter the proposed oxidation behavior.
